# UNDERWRITING MEMORANDUM — IHS Holding Limited (NYSE: IHS)

## SECTION 0 — OVERVIEW

| Item | Value | Tag |
|---|---|---|
| Ticker / Company | IHS — IHS Holding Limited (global towerco; Nigeria, SSA continuing ops post-Latam divestiture) | [Actual] |
| Price T0 (2026-10-05 live) | **$8.45** | [Actual] |
| Market cap / shares | $2.82B / 338,340,734 | [Actual] |
| **Verdict (standalone value)** | **HOLD** — Base $7.51 is 11% below price; the price is paying for deal certainty, not standalone cash flows. No crux asserted → HOLD per TASK item 6 | [Estimate] |
| Position overlay | Small momentum-basis **Accumulate** (~3% of ledger) — harness-eligible, trend backed by dated fundamental milestones | [Assumption] |

**Last complete desk run (Bear / Base / Bull):**

| Scenario | Prob. | Intrinsic value | vs T0 $8.45 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Bear | 0.15 | **$5.26** | −37.8% |
| Base | 0.55 | **$7.51** | −11.1% |
| Bull | 0.30 | **$12.41** | +46.9% |
| Probability-weighted EV | 1.00 | **$8.64** | **+2.3%** (desk) |

Margin of safety: **none on the value leg** (Base −11.1%). The stock trades ~1.3% below MTN Group's $8.50 all-cash offer (announced 2026-02-17, ~$6.2B take-private of the 75.3% MTN did not own) [Estimate — corroborated by PRIMARY P1/P6 references to the merger agreement]. Deal-inclusive expected value at my estimated 90% completion probability: 0.90 × $8.50 + 0.10 × $7.51 (standalone Base reversion) ≈ **$8.40** [Assumption] — i.e., the price implies ~95% completion certainty, and my honest estimate leaves roughly zero edge. That is why this is a trend-disciplined momentum position, not a value bet.

## SECTION 1 — MACRO

- **Rates/regime (DATA 1.5, 2026-10-04):** 10y nominal 5.24%; COE anchor 8.57%; long-run growth anchor 3.75%. Regime vector: goldilocks 0.341 headline but contested (margin 0.070); tightening 0.176, stagflation 0.130. A high-rate, contested regime is the backdrop for any standalone reversion scenario — it is why my Bear carries +100 bps on the discount rate.
- **Active shock `oil_shock` (onset 2026-09-28, severity 1, direction up) + Middle East conflict:** this is a *direct* operating input for IHS. The company's own Q2 2026 release attributes the year-on-year power-cost increase to "higher global power prices due to the conflict in the Middle East," with a one-quarter pass-through lag [Actual, PRIMARY P1]. Elevated diesel prices therefore compress standalone margins into Q3/Q4 2026 before indexation catches up — already visible (Q2 adjusted EBITDA −1.3% YoY).
- **Inflation (CPI 3.35%, PCE 3.42%, 2026-10-04):** supports the 3.75% terminal-growth default and is a mild tailwind via CPI-indexed lease escalations [Actual].
- **Deal exposure:** macro is largely irrelevant to the $8.50 cash offer itself (MTN's financing is done; IHS refinanced its maturing 2026 notes on 2026-09-09) [Actual, PRIMARY P3/P5]. Macro matters only for the standalone reversion value in a break scenario and for the carry opportunity cost while approvals complete.

## SECTION 2 — BUSINESS AND MOAT

**Economic engines (mandate 1):**

a) **Captive installed-base annuity (the core engine):** 37,672 towers with 55,205 tenants, colocation rate 1.47x, and 46,766 lease amendments at Q2 2026 [Actual, PRIMARY P1]. Long-term site leases with CPI escalation, power indexation/pass-through, and ancillary services (colocation, lease amendments, fiber). The filings show the installed base and its utilization directly — this is a contracted recurring annuity, not a projection. FY2025 segment Adjusted EBITDA: Nigeria $689.0M, SSA $298.7M [Actual, PRIMARY P2]; continuing-operations revenue Nigeria $1,068.8M / SSA $513.2M = **Nigeria ≈ 67.6% of continuing revenue** [Arithmetic on PRIMARY P2]. (The research brief's "59% Nigeria" is rejected — the filed segment table governs.)

b) **Transactional deliveries:** new-site builds and augmentation capex — FY2025 additions to PP&E/intangibles $386.4M; Q2 2026 Total Capex $39.2M, −15.2% YoY on phasing [Actual, PRIMARY P1/P2]. Cyclical with MNO capex; modest share of value.

c) **Strategic optionality:** 5G densification and colocation demand in Africa; post-deal MTN synergies (a floor for holders, not standalone value). The company has been *shrinking* its footprint — Latam ~9,000 sites sold to Macquarie (Aug 2026), I-Systems stake to TIM (May 2026), Rwanda (Oct 2025), Kuwait (Dec 2024) [Actual, PRIMARY P1] — so standalone optionality is the residual Nigerian/SSA tower book.

**Owner earnings after SBC (mandate 2):** FY2025 net income $0.144B + D&A $0.376B − capex $0.217B = **$0.302B** [Arithmetic on filed DATA 5]. SBC of $0.029B is already expensed in net income → `sbc_treatment: deducted_in_cf`, counted once. Caveat: FY2025 NI includes one-offs (gain on disposal of subsidiary $177.7M, net reversal of withholding-tax impairment $59.8M per PRIMARY P2), so the base is a filed-basis figure, not a clean run rate; the consensus year-1 level ($0.402B) is the analysts' FY2026 view.

**Moat rating (7 factors, 0–3):** installed base/switching costs **3**; market position/scale **3** (dominant Nigerian towerco, ~68% of continuing revenue); contract stickiness **2** (long leases with escalators, but FX-reset renegotiation risk); pricing power **1** (pass-throughs are cost recovery, not pricing power; Q2 EBITDA −1.3% shows input-cost sensitivity); regulatory/political **1** (emerging-market risk cuts both ways — the deal itself needed multi-country approvals); barriers to entry **2**; financial strength **1** (net leverage 2.8x [Actual, PRIMARY P1], equity −$0.251B FY2025 [Actual, DATA 6B]). **Total 13/21 → 3.5/5.0**, direction: **stable-to-softening** (divestiture-driven footprint shrink; power-cost pressure).

**Financial strength:** net debt $2.684B (vendor total debt $3.510B − cash $0.826B) [Actual, DATA 6]; consolidated net leverage 2.8x, down 0.6x YoY [Actual, PRIMARY P1]; FY2025 finance costs $436.9M vs Adjusted EBITDA $1,012.3M [Actual, PRIMARY P2]. The 2026-09-09 refinancing (irrevocable redemption of $200M 5.625% 2026 notes funded by new $200M 7.875% 2030 notes) removes the near-term maturity wall [Actual, PRIMARY P3/P5].

## SECTION 3 — VALUATION

**Frame and inputs (all passed to the desk; equity frame because every flow in the pack is after interest):**

| Input | Value | Departure from DEFAULTS? | Reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| base_cf (Base) | $0.302B | No — DEFAULTS owner earnings (FY2025 filed basis) | Within 2% of default; no reason needed |
| Base explicit growth y1–y5 | +33.1%, −14.4%, −3.0%, −3.0%, −3.0% | No — reproduces consensus levels y1 $0.402B, y2 $0.344B (within 5%), then next-FY revenue growth −3.0% for y3–5 | No `guidance_deviation_reason` needed |
| Discount rate (Base/Bull) | 8.57% | No — COE ANCHOR | — |
| Discount rate (Bear) | 9.57% | +100 bps scenario shock | Mandate 4 cost-of-capital stress; tightening regime probability 0.176 |
| terminal_g | 3.75% | No — DEFAULTS (own FY2019–25 revenue trend 4.31%/yr, held between breakeven inflation 2.36% and anchor) | — |
| terminal_ronic | 8.57% | No — DEFAULTS = COE; record's median r_tc is −20.4% (below COE), so new investment earns only its cost — conservative, record-supported | — |
| fade_years | 5 | Default structure | — |
| Shares | 338,340,734 | No — DEFAULTS (no dilution factor measurable: no period with |EPS| ≥ $0.50) | — |
| Cash-flow life | Perpetual | — | Installed base of 37,672 towers is renewed/expanded out of capex already deducted in the flows (Q2 2026 capex $39.2M; FY2025 additions $386.4M); no finite reserve, licence or concession term [Actual, PRIMARY P1/P2] |
| Excess cash | $0 (default) | No | With net leverage 2.8x the $0.826B cash is operating/debt-service liquidity, not excess; its interest income is already in net income and the offsetting debt's interest already deducted — adding face value would double-count. The Base result ($7.51) sits within 0.3% of the consensus-implied reference ($7.53), which uses the same treatment |
| SBC | deducted_in_cf | Declared | Counted once (already in NI) |

**Desk terminal:** g 3.75%, ronic 8.57%; implied terminal multiple **21.5x funded FCF** (Base/Bull), 17.8x (Bear); terminal is ~30% of Base value. Cross-check vs the MRI real_estate trailing-P/E band (median 23.2x, p25 10.5x, p75 47.9x): different metric (EV/funded-FCF vs P/E), but 21.5x sits below the sector P/E median and inside the p25–p75 band — no extreme stretch [Estimate, DATA 8.5].

**Reverse DCF (mandate 3b):**
- *Neutral structure* (anchor COE 8.57%, terminal g 3.75%, 10-year fade): solved initial growth **−16.7%**, implied **10-year CAGR −5.63%** → **below p50** of the $1–10B base-rate bucket (median +4.7%/10y, +5.6%/5y).
- *My structure:* implied stage-1 growth **+3.71%**/yr vs demonstrated 5y revenue CAGR +2.4% — IN-LINE, expectations gap +1.3 pts.
- **Argument:** the neutral reverse DCF says the market prices in a *shrinking* standalone business. That is consistent with the filings: the company has divested Latam (~9,000 sites), I-Systems, Rwanda and Kuwait; Q2 2026 organic revenue growth was only +0.5% (constant currency +2.2%) with adjusted EBITDA −1.3% [Actual, PRIMARY P1]. The price is not paying for standalone growth — it is paying for the $8.50 cash floor. That is why I assert **no crux**: the price is set by a pending offer, not by a fundamentals mispricing to be exploited. (For completeness: at my inputs the price would equal the Base only if terminal_ronic were 16.3% — double what the company's 7-year record supports (median r_tc −20.4%) — but that "disagreement" is an artifact of valuing a deal-arb with a DCF, not evidence the price is wrong on standalone merits.)

**Pending-offer overlay (TASK item 1):** Standalone EV $8.64 (desk). With the offer at my estimated **90% completion probability** [Assumption — see SECTION 5 evidence]: 0.90 × $8.50 + 0.10 × $7.51 ≈ **$8.40**; at 95%: $8.45 = price (the implied probability). Verdict stays on standalone value: **HOLD**.

## SECTION 4 — SCENARIOS (last complete desk run, exactly as returned)

| **Bear** | 0.15 | **$5.26** | −37.8% | Oil shock (onset 2026-09-28) + Middle East conflict keep diesel elevated; the one-quarter pass-through lag becomes persistent (Q2 2026 already showed +$35.3M YoY power costs [Actual, PRIMARY P1]); FX resets bite on Nigeria (~68% of continuing revenue); a deal break forces standalone reversion in a tightening regime → COE shocked to 9.57%; cash flow −10%/−8% in y1–y2 fading to −2%. |
| **Base** | 0.55 | **$7.51** | −11.1% | Consensus path: FY2026 owner earnings $0.402B → FY2027 $0.344B → −3%/yr (next-FY revenue growth) y3–5; 5-year fade to 3.75%; power pass-through catches up with the one-quarter lag; colocation grows modestly from 1.47x. |
| **Bull** | 0.30 | **$12.41** | +46.9% | FY2025 ALFCF of $448.1M (+47.3% YoY) [Actual, company 4QFY25 release] was achievable on a continuing basis if power costs normalize: colocation compounds from 1.47x, 46,766 lease amendments and CPI escalations drive +2–6%/yr cash-flow growth; Naira stable (0.1% QoQ in Q2 2026 [Actual, PRIMARY P1]). |

**Probabilities justified:** Base 55% — the consensus path is modal and my Base matches the analysts' own earnings path within 0.3%. Bull 30% — the company's own FY2025 ALFCF print plus a stable Naira supports a higher run rate if the power shock fades. Bear 15% — the active oil shock, the pass-through lag, and residual SSA approval risk make a break-plus-impairment outcome real but not likely (largest market cleared conditionally; MTN publicly committed to H2 2026).

**Contracted-floor check:** the filings show the installed base (37,672 towers / 55,205 tenants) and colocation rate [Actual, PRIMARY P1] but no dollar backlog figure; the Bear's −10% year-1 cut models churn/renegotiation within a durable annuity, not cancellation — no floor is breached.

## SECTION 7 — RISKS

- **Delay, not break:** residual SSA approvals (Cameroon, Côte d'Ivoire) slipping past H2 2026 → spread earned over a longer horizon; price drifts down from the offer.
- **Deal break/renegotiation:** reversion to standalone Base $7.51 (−11%) or Bear $5.26 (−38%); Q2 2026's $7.5M net loss shows standalone earnings power is thinner than the offer implies [Actual, PRIMARY P1].
- **Power costs:** oil shock + Middle East conflict keep diesel elevated; one-quarter pass-through lag means continued compression into Q3/Q4 2026 [Actual, PRIMARY P1].
- **FX:** Nigeria ≈ 68% of continuing revenue; Q2 2026's +$40.7M translation tailwind from Naira appreciation can reverse; FX resets under some contracts cut the other way [Actual, PRIMARY P1].
- **Leverage/regime:** 2.8x net leverage, negative equity, high-rate contested regime (tightening probability 0.176) makes standalone refinancing expensive in a break scenario.
- **Conditions:** Nigeria's 30% sell-down and SA fair-access/operational-independence conditions trim MTN's strategic value and add integration friction — a latent renegotiation trigger, though unlikely to block.

**Pre-mortem (−50% in five years):** two SSA regulators rejected the deal in early 2027; the stock gapped toward $7.50 and then the standalone business compounded at negative cash-flow growth — power costs never fully passed through, the Naira depreciated ~15%, MNOs renegotiated leases under FX stress, and leverage stayed above 3x so de-levering stalled. By 2031 the stock trades at or below Bear-case $5.26: a ~38% loss plus forfeited carry.

## SECTION 9 — RED TEAM

**Strongest short thesis:** "The easy money was made in February. At $8.45 vs $8.50 there is only ~1.3% of spread left, and the price implies ~95% completion certainty. Remaining SSA approvals can slip into 2027 — the spread is then earned over a longer horizon and the price trades down from the offer. If the deal breaks, standalone support is far below $8.50: Q2 2026 was a $7.5M net loss with EBITDA down on power costs, the company has been selling its best assets (Latam ~9,000 sites, I-Systems, Rwanda), and what remains is a shrinking annuity at 2.8x leverage in a high-rate regime. The offer was only a modest premium — MTN has no incentive to improve it."

**My answer:** the short thesis is largely right about the *thin carry* — which is exactly why this is not a Strong Buy and the value verdict is HOLD. But the dated evidence shows completion risk *falling*, not rising: the largest market (Nigeria, ~68% of continuing revenue) is cleared conditionally, South Africa and Zambia are cleared, shareholders approved (EGM, August 2026), the 2026 maturity wall was refinanced into 2030 paper (2026-09-09), and MTN has publicly committed to H2 2026. The residual risk is delay (managed by the 10%-below-high break rule), not break; and on a break, standalone Base is $7.51 (−11%), not the −38% Bear, which additionally requires sustained power-cost and FX impairment. At p(deal) = 90%, EV ≈ $8.40 ≈ price: this is a small momentum trade with a defined exit, not a value position — sized accordingly.
